questions.question: Explain why Hitler was able to remilitarise the Rhineland in 1936. (4 marks)

points.text: Hitler was able to remilitarise the Rhineland because: France was in political crisis and would not act without British support; Britain believed Germany was "only going into its own back garden"; Britain was distracted by the Abyssinian crisis; the League of Nations was discredited; and Hitler offered "peace proposals" to appear reasonable. questions.question: How important was the policy of appeasement in allowing Hitler to achieve his foreign policy aims? (8 marks)

points.text: Appeasement was crucial in allowing Hitler's successes. At each stage - Rhineland (1936), Anschluss (1938), Sudetenland (1938) - Britain and France chose not to resist. questions.question: "The Munich Agreement was a mistake." How far do you agree? (12 marks)

points.text: The Munich Agreement was a mistake because: it gave Hitler the Sudetenland without a fight, making him stronger; Czechoslovakia lost its defensive fortifications and was left defenceless; it proved Hitler could not be trusted - within 6 months he had seized the rest of Czechoslovakia; it encouraged Hitler to make further demands (Poland); and it undermined the credibility of Britain and France. questions.question: "Hitler's foreign policy was the main cause of the Second World War." How far do you agree? (16 marks)

points.text: Hitler's foreign policy was a major cause of WWII because he deliberately set out to destroy the Versailles settlement, unite all Germans, and conquer Lebensraum. Each move - Rhineland, Anschluss, Sudetenland, Czechoslovakia, Poland - escalated towards war.
